tender.title: Telemetry Engineering Support Services
tender.description:
Scottish Water is establishing a Framework Agreement for Telemetry Engineering Support Services, covering the survey, supply, installation, commissioning, decommissioning and documentation of Remote Telemetry Units (RTUs) and associated communications equipment across Scottish Water's water and wastewater asset base, together with reactive telemetry support. Services may be required anywhere in Scotland, so Suppliers must be able to service all geographic areas.

The scope includes, but is not limited to:

- Desktop and on-site surveys of existing and future telemetry installations, including communications surveys (e.g. 4G, SOGEA, FTTP).
- Procurement of RTUs and associated equipment through Scottish Water's mandatory RTU framework, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) prior to delivery to site.
- Supply and installation of RTU associated communications equipment in accordance with Scottish Water specifications (antennas, surge and lightning protection, cable containment, marshalling, relays, signal conditioners, Modbus PLC communications, data gatherers and inter-site comms).
- Programming and end to end (source to screen) commissioning and testing of new and existing plant monitored by the telemetry top end, including hot swaps of live RTUs.
- Decommissioning of RTUs and associated equipment, including safe removal, return of spares and WEEE compliant disposal.
- Production of IO tag sheets, mimics, risk assessments and method statements, commissioning and FAT records, Ready to Go Live documentation and Operation and Maintenance manuals, in line with Scottish Water procedures and a Common Data Environment aligned to ISO 19650.
- Training for Scottish Water Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) support staff on installed telemetry.
- Additional on-site support to Scottish Water E&M teams for communications failures, reactive faults and minor enhancements, and to supplement Scottish Water maintenance teams during periods of high breakdown volumes or staff shortages.

Work will be delivered on assets within Scottish Water's Operational Technology environment, which is in scope of the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations, in accordance with Scottish Water's Telemetry Realisation Process, telemetry procedures and Engineering Specification Section 633 - Telemetry. The Supplier will act as Principal Contractor only and must provide its own base facilities, as Scottish Water will not make premises available.

Call-off contracts will be awarded under the Framework by direct allocation or mini-competition. Scottish Water may appoint more than one Supplier. Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee any volume or value of work.

This opportunity is aimed at telemetry, SCADA, instrumentation and controls and electrical engineering contractors with proven capability in delivering telemetry installations on operational water and wastewater assets, a competent and suitably qualified workforce, and the capacity to respond across Scotland.

lots.description:
Scottish Water is seeking to appoint Suppliers to a Framework Agreement for the provision of Telemetry Engineering Support Services. The Framework will support the survey, supply, installation, commissioning, decommissioning and documentation of Remote Telemetry Units (RTUs) and associated communications equipment on Scottish Water's water and wastewater assets, for both new and existing works, together with reactive telemetry support to Scottish Water's Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) teams.

Services may be required across all of Scotland. Suppliers must therefore be able to service all geographic areas of Scotland.

This notice is intended to help prospective Suppliers understand the nature and breadth of the services so that those with the right capability and capacity can decide whether to participate.

The scope of services includes, but is not limited to, the following.

Surveys

- Desktop and on-site surveys of existing telemetry installations.
- Desktop and on-site surveys for future telemetry installations.
- Communications surveys (desktop and on site) to establish the communications options available for future installations and to document existing communications (e.g. 4G, SOGEA, FTTP).
- Surveys will identify hazards and limitations relevant to the telemetry installation, its function and site access, and will record the location, type and function of the RTU and its associated communications equipment, any integration with control systems (PLC and SCADA), the electrical supply, cable ways and marshalling arrangements.

Remote Telemetry Units and associated equipment

- Procurement of Framework approved RTUs and associated equipment via Scottish Water's approved supply chain. Use of Scottish Water's RTU framework (currently SW20/CI/1285/1 - Supply of Remote Telemetry Units, or any successor or replacement framework) is mandatory.
- Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of RTUs before delivery to site.
- Supply and installation of RTU associated communications equipment in accordance with Scottish Water specifications, including antennas, surge protection, lightning protection, cable containment, marshalling junction boxes, knife edge terminations, relays, signal conditioners (24v / 0-20mA), PLC communication via RS485 Modbus protocol, 230v unswitched fused spurs, data gatherers and inter-site communications.
- Where ancillary electrical work is required, design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning in compliance with BS 7671, the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and applicable UK water industry standards, including relevant WIMES, Scottish Water specifications and Sewers for Scotland.

Programming, testing and commissioning

- Programming of RTUs and completion of the IO and mimic configuration based on Scottish Water design packages.
- End to end (source to screen) commissioning of all new and existing plant monitored by the telemetry top end, including hot swaps of live RTUs and signal additions or modifications, in collaboration with Scottish Water's Telemetry Engineering Support Team (TeST) and Specialist Service Delivery (SSD) team.
- Close liaison with Scottish Water Operations, principal partners and control centre staff to plan and coordinate testing.

Decommissioning

- Decommissioning of telemetry RTUs and associated equipment. Equipment is to be removed from site unless otherwise instructed, with any equipment left in place made safe and labelled.
- Return of spares to Scottish Water where instructed, and safe disposal of removed equipment in accordance with WEEE and other relevant legislation.
- Removal and making safe of redundant power supplies, RTU cards and cabling, and updating of enclosure labelling where existing enclosures are reused.

Documentation and information management

- Production of IO tag sheets and mimics based on the design package provided by Scottish Water or its partners.
- Risk assessments and method statements in compliance with Scottish Water requirements.
- Testing documentation, including commissioning records and FAT documentation.
- Ready to Go Live (RtGL) documentation in accordance with Scottish Water SSD and TeST procedures and standards.
- Operations and Maintenance (O&M) manuals in accordance with Scottish Water procedures and standards.
- Compliance with Scottish Water's Common Data Environment requirements for the SR27 regulatory period (Autodesk Forma), including alignment to ISO 19650, naming conventions, metadata, folder structures, workflows and product data.

Training

- Training for local Scottish Water E&M support staff on the telemetry RTU installed, including anything non-standard or specific to the site, rather than generic manufacturer information only.

Maintenance and reactive support

- Additional support to Scottish Water's E&M department as required for communications failures, reactive faults and minor enhancements.
- On-site telemetry support to supplement Scottish Water's own maintenance teams during periods of high breakdown volumes or staff shortages.

Project management and reporting

- Monthly financial and programme reporting.
- Applications for payment in line with the Scottish Water payment calendar.
- The Supplier will act as Principal Contractor only and will be assessed as such by Scottish Water.
- Working to Scottish Water processes and procedures, including the Telemetry Realisation Process and telemetry procedures that form part of the scope documents.
- A defect period of 2 years.

DELIVERY ENVIRONMENT AND EXPECTATIONS

Telemetry and operational technology

The services will be delivered on telemetry equipment, RTUs, communications infrastructure and PLC interfaces that form part of Scottish Water's Operational Technology (OT) environment, which is in scope of the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations. Suppliers will be expected to work to secure-by-design principles and Scottish Water's OT security requirements.

Standards and specifications

Work must comply with Scottish Water's Standards and Specifications, including Engineering Specification Section 633 - Telemetry.

Geographic coverage and base operations

Suppliers must be capable of servicing all geographic areas of Scotland. Scottish Water will not make premises available for Suppliers to establish base operations, so Suppliers must have sufficient facilities to service the Framework. Same day attendance at mainland sites within 150 miles of the Supplier's Scottish base (or the Central Belt if there is no Scottish base) is expected as a minimum.

Workforce competence

All personnel must be appropriately trained, qualified and experienced, and able to work to industry-recognised health, safety and quality standards. This includes, but is not limited to, CSCS / Electrical Safety Certification Scheme, DOMS, Water Hygiene, Confined Space and Working at Height training.

Working with Scottish Water teams

Suppliers will work closely with Scottish Water's SSD and TeST teams and other Scottish Water framework partners and will be expected to meet defined service levels and lead times throughout the telemetry delivery process.

Work will be awarded through call-off contracts under the Framework Agreement, by either direct allocation or mini-competition depending on the nature of the individual work package. Scottish Water may appoint more than one Supplier to the Framework.

Where work is directly allocated, Scottish Water may consider factors such as resource capacity and competence, telemetry device and site experience, performance, quotation and specific stakeholder or project requirements. Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee any minimum volume, value or share of work. Scottish Water Horizons Limited may also use the Framework where it is an entitled user.

This opportunity is aimed at organisations with proven experience of delivering telemetry, SCADA, instrumentation and controls and electrical engineering services on operational water, wastewater or other critical infrastructure assets, and which can demonstrate:

- Experience of surveying, installing, programming and commissioning RTU based telemetry systems.
- A competent, suitably qualified workforce and the resource capacity to deliver across Scotland.
- The ability to produce high quality technical documentation and manage information in a Common Data Environment.
- Capability to operate as Principal Contractor.
- A strong commitment to health and safety and to working collaboratively with Scottish Water and its wider supply chain.

Full details of the requirements, including the scope documents, Telemetry Realisation Process and Standards and Specifications, will be available to participating Bidders through the Scottish Water e-Sourcing portal (Atamis). Profitability – this is taken as profit after tax but before dividends and minority interests. If a company makes a profit then it is a pass for this ratio;
Liquidity – this is calculated as current assets less stock and work in progress, divided by current liabilities. If the answer is greater than or equal to one then it is a pass for this ratio
Gearing – this is calculated as the total external secured borrowing (short term and long term) divided by shareholder funds expressed as a percentage. If the answer is less than or equal to 100% it is considered a pass for this ratio.
Bidders must provide the name and value of each of the 3 ratios within their response to SPD question 4B.4.
The Council requires bidders to pass 2 out of the 3 financial ratios above.

Would the bidder have passed the checks if prior year accounts had been used?

tender.description: Islington Council is re-opening its flexible framework agreement for the procurement and management of nightly purchased accommodation.  We invite suitable expressions of interest from suppliers interested in working alongside us to deliver this essential service.

lots.description:
Background
The Council had over 2,000 homeless households living in temporary accommodation as of 30 September 2026.  The purpose of the service is to ensure homeless clients are housed in suitable, good quality, secure and safe accommodation that meets the standards as set out in in the procurement documentation.  Clients will be supported to participate and engage/re-engage with the community, tackle worklessness and contribute to the local community.
The requirement
To ensure the provision of nightly purchased accommodation can match the demands of the Housing Needs service and promote the provision of high-quality accommodation for the residents of Islington.
The Council has a statutory duty towards under the homelessness legislation as laid down in the 1985 and 1996 Housing Acts and the 2017 Homelessness Reduction Act.  The ready supply of accommodation will also allow the Council to fulfil its duties under the Care Act and Children’s Act, and offering temporary accommodation to clients who have No Recourse to Public Funds (NRPF).
Providers will be responsible for delivering the supply of properties that are local to Islington.  For the purpose of this contract opportunity, the Council defines a local property as a property that is:
•	in the borough of Islington;
•	located in a neighbouring borough i.e. Hackney, Camden, Haringey; and/or
•	is accessible to Islington via public transport with a journey time no longer than one hour.
Our mission is to create a more equal Islington, where everyone who lives here has the opportunity and an equal chance to thrive. We are all at the heart of driving this forward. But it’s not just what we do, it’s the way that we do it. This is underpinned by four values which spell out ‘CARE’ and represent what we think public service is all about: being Collaborative, Ambitious, Resourceful and Empowering.
This service supports the Council’s objectives to:
•	support people experiencing homelessness
•	reduce rough sleeping in the borough
•	ensure decent and safe accommodation
•	challenge inequality
There is no maximum number of providers that will be party to the framework agreement.  Call-off contracts from the framework agreement shall follow the terms of the framework agreement including how a call-off contract is concluded.  How a call-off contract is concluded is explained within the procurement documentation. Additional information: Lots
This framework agreement is not split into lots as the Council’s sole requirement is for providers of nightly purchased accommodation.
TUPE [Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations]
TUPE does not apply to this opportunity.
Procurement Process
The procurement is subject to the ‘light-touch regime’ under Section 7 Social and Other Specific Services of Part 2 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (the PCR). Under Regulation 76 the Council is free to establish its own procurement procedure, provided that the procedure is sufficient to ensure compliance with the principles of transparency and equal treatment of economic operators (service providers) and is initiated by a contract notice.
The process that has been developed for this procurement considers the unique nature of this market and has been designed so as to fully utilise the flexibility provided by the services falling within the ‘light-touch regime’.
Further details are available in the procurement documents.

- are independent and professional;
- provide individual (one-to-one) advocacy that is issue focused; and
- meet statutory requirements and Scottish Executive priorities.
The service will covers such services under the following categories:
- Advocacy services for children and young people who are or have been looked after and accommodated within or outwith the region (excluding those who are placed locally by another Local Authority) up until the age of 26.
- Advocacy for children and young people on the Child Protection Register.
- Advocacy for children and young people in terms of the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003.

lots.description:
This procurement is to obtain a suitable advocacy service provider for children's advocacy services. The service objectives are as follows:
To provide an independent and confidential advocacy service to include information, support and advice for Dumfries and Galloway children and young people who are or have been looked after and accommodated within or outwith the region.
To provide access to an advocacy service for children & young people regardless of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, faith/religion, or social background.
To match service users and advocates appropriate to each situation’s needs, seeking specialist support where indicated and ensuring service users comfort at all times.
To ensure that children & young people’s own views are heard and adequately represented.
To provide advocacy, related support and information in an age-appropriate and child/young person-centred manner.
To help children and young people to access and understand information relevant to them and make appropriate choices or decisions which give them fuller control of their lives.
To promote choices to young people.
To support children & young people who, because of incapacity or communication difficulties, may not be able to express their needs or views.
To provide advocacy for children and young people who have a mental disorder in compliance with the Mental Health Act.
To guide children and young people towards self-advocacy and avoid creation of dependency.
To develop links with service providers, professionals and relevant support organisations to ensure clear understanding of the role of advocacy.
To develop and promote children and young people’s involvement in service planning.

tender.title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services
tender.description:
The demand for accessible, high-quality and innovative sexual health services continues to evolve in response to changing population needs, advances in clinical practice, increasing digital delivery models and the ongoing focus on reducing health inequalities.
The Framework will provide Relevant Authorities with a fully compliant route for the provision of sexual health services, supporting the commissioning of integrated, digital, clinical, diagnostic, prevention, outreach and specialist support services. The Framework is designed to enable Contracting Authorities to secure services that improve public health outcomes, promote early intervention and prevention, support vulnerable populations, and ensure equitable access to care. 
The overall aim of the Framework is to provide a compliant route to market facilitating the procurement of various Sexual Health Services. 
The Framework has been established under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 and The Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025 (and as amended) (together the PSR) for use by all Relevant Authorities (and any future successors to these organisations).
"Relevant Authority" is defined in section 12ZB(7) of the National Health Service Act 2006 and in section 10A(9) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. It means a combined authority, an integrated care board, a local authority in England, NHS England, an NHS foundation trust or an NHS trust established under section 25 of the National Health Service Act 2006, a county council or county borough council in Wales, a local health board established under section 11 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, a National Health Service trust established under section 18 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, or a special health authority established under section 22 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. 
For the avoidance of doubt, any successor bodies of any of the above entities shall be entitled to place Orders and shall be deemed Relevant Authorities for the purposes of this Framework.
The Framework will be re-opened to new applicants every two years, approximately 90 days before the anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date.
